canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick, Volume 1: 1938–1971
author: Philip K. Dick (edited by Don Herron; introduction by James Blaylock)
card_summary: The Underwood-Miller volume covering 1938-1971, edited by Don Herron with an introduction by James Blaylock, spanning PKD's boyhood letters to his mother through the Berkeley marriages and the drug-strained end of the 1960s.
page_summary:
This first volume of the Selected Letters reaches furthest back, gathering correspondence from 1938 to 1971, edited by Don Herron with an introduction by James Blaylock. It opens with the boyhood and adolescent letters, including those written home from the California Preparatory School in Ojai, that are among the earliest substantial PKD prose to survive, and carries through his Berkeley years, his early marriages, and his emergence as a working science-fiction novelist.

The letters document the long apprenticeship and mid-career of a writer largely before the visionary turn: his dealings with agents and editors, the composition and reception of novels including The Man in the High Castle, his classical-music passions, and the mounting personal instability of the late 1960s.

As the volume covering more than three decades, it is the primary correspondence source for PKD's life before 2-3-74, from the childhood record through the drug-era crises that closed the 1960s.
